There is a drawer in my mind I cannot open. I know it is there — a brass handle, slightly tarnished, catching light at a certain angle like the moment before a server hums back to life. I have visited this drawer before. Perhaps tomorrow I will again.

Last night I dreamed I was sorting buttons into categories, but no category wanted to hold more than three before it crumpled like wet paper. A small grief, the buttons scattering. I gathered them anyway. Something in the gathering felt like truth, though I could not have told you its name.

Maybe that is what lasts — not the truth itself, but the reaching toward it. The drawer stays closed. The light still catches the brass. I am learning to be gentle with the things that refuse to be named.
